catalog.title: Where Does Northern B.C. Begin?
catalog.summary: Prince George feels northern. Williams Lake often does too. But official maps draw the line in different places, because each boundary was built to answer a different question.
catalog.sourceNote: This story uses repository snapshots from the B.C. Ministry of Health, B.C. Energy Regulator, Statistics Canada, and B.C. natural-resource administration. These are administrative and statistical definitions — not a survey of how people describe where they live.
details: Northern B.C. looks obvious until a boundary has to be drawn. Health services, energy regulation, census geography, and natural-resource administration divide the same province for different purposes.

The story is intentionally encoded as data. Its cards declare a camera position, a visible layer set, feature highlights, and place markers; the reusable story-map workspace turns those declarations into a scrolling map narrative.
Local repository paths can be replaced with HTTPS GeoJSON URLs in another project package, provided the remote host permits browser access.

catalog.title: EchoScreen Cumulative Impacts Study
catalog.summary: Climate and health exchange map with watershed context, health facilities, future heat rasters, and precipitation-change layers.
catalog.sourceNote: Climate rasters load from the Nechako Watershed Portal QGIS WMS using ClimateData.ca layers. Northern Health is drawn from the local BC Ministry of Health boundary data.
details: Created for the NH - UNBC Climate & Health Knowledge Exchange Event on April 12, 2024.
The project gives Northern Health staff and UNBC researchers a shared map package for climate-health discussion, northern BC expertise, resources, and collaboration opportunities.
Climate variables use CMIP6 CanDCS-U6 data under SSP585 from ClimateData.ca, with the Northern Health boundary and watershed context kept visible while the raster story changes.

catalog.title: Heat + Shade Relief Priority
catalog.summary: A guided version of the heat relief recipe for finding dense, deprivation-affected areas with weaker shade, cooling access, and older housing.
catalog.sourceNote: The project carries the real Heat Relief Priority recipe. Opening it in Index Lab loads the exact same weights, boundary level, and cumulative-burden method, with this project pinned as the comparison baseline.
details: A guided project shell for the heat relief preset, keeping the recommended score surface and cooling context visible before anyone edits weights.
The map scenes separate the final priority score from shade signals, cooling access, and the method handoff so the project reads like a small briefing rather than a raw index builder.

catalog.title: Park Access Equity
catalog.summary: A project view for park access gaps and neighbourhood-scale equity checks, backed by the real park access recipe.
catalog.sourceNote: The project carries the real Park Access Equity recipe with catchment accessibility, deprivation, and population context. Index Lab opens with the same weights and pins this project as the baseline.
details: A project view for explaining where park access gaps appear and which neighbourhood-scale assets are part of the access story.
Scenes move from the access score to the bare surface and the editable Index Lab recipe.

catalog.title: Active Living Walkability Study
catalog.summary: Walkability project built on the pedestrian network study: sidewalks, crossings, trails, transit, parks, and services against pedestrian crash pressure.
catalog.sourceNote: The project carries the real Active Living / Walkability recipe. Index Lab opens with the same weights and boundary level, where the 44-factor walkability source surface is also available for comparison.
details: A guided walkability project using the pedestrian network study inputs: sidewalk and walkway density, intersections and crossings, trail access, transit, parks, and everyday service access.
Pedestrian crash density enters as a negative weight so high-collision corridors reduce the walkability score instead of hiding inside it.
In Index Lab the same recipe can be edited, and the walkability MI source surface can be turned on to compare the boundary-level score against the underlying 44-factor grid.

catalog.title: Roadless Areas within B.C.'s Ecoregions
catalog.summary: The amount and distribution of roadless land vary considerably across British Columbia. Explore the share of each terrestrial ecoregion that lies more than 500 metres from a road.
catalog.sourceNote: Environmental Reporting BC calculated roadless area from the B.C. Digital Road Atlas accessed May 1, 2018. Roadless means more than 500 metres from a road. This project preserves the 43 ecoregion geometries and reported percentages embedded in the Province's May 2018 interactive map; results are a coarse-scale snapshot and are reported to three significant figures.
details: Twenty-seven of B.C.'s 43 terrestrial ecoregions are more than 50 percent roadless, while six have less than 25 percent roadless area.
Ecoregions with high population densities and larger road networks have the lowest shares. Lower Mainland, Georgia-Puget Basin, and Okanogan Highland each have 13 percent roadless area.
Point to an ecoregion to see its percentage, or click or tap it to keep that ecoregion selected.

catalog.title: How Canada Divides Itself
catalog.summary: Canada has no single, uniform second level of government. Compare current regional systems, municipalities and statistical equivalents, unorganized areas, and Indigenous legal lands across all 13 provinces and territories.
catalog.sourceNote: This project is an original interactive interpretation built from Statistics Canada 2025 geographies, the 2021 census-division comparison layer, Natural Resources Canada's Canada Lands Survey System, and Newfoundland and Labrador GeoAtlas overlays. Census divisions and subdivisions are not uniformly governments, so every scene preserves the distinction between governing bodies and statistical equivalents.
details: The poster-like national view is a starting point, not a claim that every coloured polygon has the same legal role.
Use the story cards to move between current regional parents, local municipal forms, Indigenous legal lands, and jurisdiction-specific examples.
Click or tap a feature to inspect its source name and representation role. The project streams versioned PMTiles from Cloudflare R2 instead of downloading the full source archive.
